name: Tiger Pipeline Richland Parish Lateral (Entergy Louisiana, Meta Hyperion supply)
researcher_notes: Energy Transfer and Entergy Louisiana signed a 20-year firm transport deal in November 2025. A 12-mile lateral off the Tiger Pipeline, up to 1 billion cubic feet per day, serves new Entergy gas plants and Meta's data center in Richland Parish. Trade press (Pipeline and Gas Journal, November 2025) names the lateral and the Meta data center. The Energy Information Administration August 2026 pipeline projects table (sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Excel row 123, listed as Tiger Pipeline Expansion Project) gives 12 miles, 1,000 million cubic feet per day, proposed, in service 2028, intrastate, and ties it to Entergy Louisiana's data center power plant. The Entergy press release was read and also describes the agreement. This is not P5849 (the operating 2011 Tiger expansion) and not P0265 (the main line). It is new pipe, so it is its own row. Start location was not stated by a source, so it is left blank. Delhi comes from the trade press as the delivery point. Capacity is 1,000 million cubic feet per day as the maximum; the firm contract is 250,000 MMBtu per day. Diameter, owner entity and cost were not found. The company holding the pipe is probably a Tiger Pipeline subsidiary of Energy Transfer, but no source names it, so Owner is left blank for the ownership team. A 13.24 mile figure from a FERC filing seen by one search was not verified and no FERC filing was found; EIA lists it as intrastate. Route not researched. Tier high: two independent sources agree on length and capacity. DataCenter is yes because trade press and EIA both name the Meta/Entergy data center supply.
